registry.description: Mourning is the outward expression of inner grief — the practices, gestures, and sounds through which sorrow makes itself known in the world. The Hebrew vocabulary here covers sitting in ashes, tearing garments, wailing, and the professional mourning practices of the ancient world. Mourning is honoured in Scripture as the appropriate response to real loss: Jesus mourns, the psalmists mourn, Lamentations is an entire book of mourning. The Beatitudes name the mourning as those who will be comforted. Mourning is not the failure of faith but its expression.
